safety.confidence_note: Rabbit does not bind brolucizumab pharmacologically; the inflammation is a product/immunogenic harm the species can show. Pre-GMP pilot batch presumed.
safety.note: Single 500 ug/eye intravitreal brolucizumab gave severe ocular inflammation in 4/36 rabbits (report dated Dec 2010); no patient data yet.
safety.quote: Severe ocular inflammation was observed in 4/36 rabbits treated at a single dose-level, 500 μg/eye
safety.judgement: Opening entry at the 2010 study; the review also notes GMP lots 'continued to cause infrequent severe ocular inflammation in monkeys and rabbits'.

safety.magnitude_basis: intraocular inflammation incidence (rabbit 4/36 eyes; patients 4% vs 1% aflibercept)
safety.confidence_note: Pairing (comparison_stated false): label adverse-reaction table gives IOI 4% vs 1%; FDA reviewer did not link rabbit findings to patients.
safety.note: Patients had excess intraocular inflammation (4% vs 1% on aflibercept), the harm the rabbit studies showed.
safety.quote: Intraocular inflammation was observed in 6% of patients with anti-brolucizumab antibodies detected during dosing with BEOVU.
safety.reason: rabbit IOI matched excess patient IOI
safety.judgement: Separate track from the draft's monkey toxicology (which saw no effects in the pivotal study); the rabbit signal was attributed to pre-GMP material, but the review says GMP lots also caused it, so scored as a stated harm that recurred in patients.

added_models.model: Mechanistic multi-compartment ocular PK model, rabbit-scaled to human (abicipar)

dose.model: Mechanistic multi-compartment ocular PK model, rabbit-scaled to human (abicipar)
dose.confidence_note: First-use year 2015 is a proxy (model simulated the proposed phase 3 regimens; CEDAR/SEQUOIA began 2015).
dose.note: Rabbit ocular PK scaled to a human model simulated vitreal abicipar above VEGF IC50 under 2 mg Q8/Q12, supporting phase 3 regimens.
dose.quote: Thus, predictions for human PK by multi-compartment PK model support dose selection and treatment regimen of 2 mg/eye 2Q8/2Q12.

dose.model: Mechanistic multi-compartment ocular PK model, rabbit-scaled to human (abicipar)
dose.magnitude_basis: abicipar serum and aqueous humor concentrations
dose.confidence_note: Regulator summary only; the sponsor model report is not public, no fold-error stated.
dose.note: EMA states the human-scaled model fitted measured serum and aqueous abicipar in nAMD/DME patients; patient data were used in the scaling.
dose.short: Human PK model fitted patient data
dose.quote: After scaling this data to the human model using aqueous und serum data, the human model again fitted well against the measured abicipar concentrations in serum and aqueous humor from patients with nAMD and diabetic macular edema, respectively.
dose.reason: fit to patient PK used in scaling
dose.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the human model was scaled using patient aqueous and serum data, so its fit is a retrodiction.

efficacy.model: Mechanistic multi-compartment ocular PK model, rabbit-scaled to human (abicipar)
efficacy.note: Model predicted complete vitreal VEGF suppression over 52 weeks under 2 mg Q8 and Q12 regimens.
efficacy.short: Predicted full VEGF suppression on Q12
efficacy.quote: Additionally, complete suppression of VEGF concentrations were predicted over the same time period.

efficacy.model: Mechanistic multi-compartment ocular PK model, rabbit-scaled to human (abicipar)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: stable vision at week 52 on Q12 vs monthly ranibizumab
efficacy.confidence_note: Pairing; Ophthalmology abstract read. registry_date copied from the draft's CEDAR entry.
efficacy.note: CEDAR/SEQUOIA: abicipar Q8 and Q12 were non-inferior to monthly ranibizumab, as the predicted sustained suppression implied.
efficacy.quote: Abicipar Q8 and Q12 were both noninferior to ranibizumab Q4 in the primary end point of stable vision at week 52.
efficacy.judgement: The model's simulation was prospective for phase 3 regimens even though its human scaling used phase 2 PK; IOI is scored on the draft's toxicology track, not here.

added_models.model: Rat subretinal/suprachoroidal RGX-314 with VEGF-induced vascular leakage

engagement.model: Rat subretinal/suprachoroidal RGX-314 with VEGF-induced vascular leakage
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. First-use year is the first public date; the rat work likely predates the 2017 phase 1 start.
engagement.note: In rats, subretinal or suprachoroidal RGX-314 expressed anti-VEGF Fab and suppressed VEGF-induced leakage.
engagement.quote: Compared with subretinal injection in rats of RGX-314, an AAV8 vector expressing an anti-VEGF Fab, suprachoroidal injection of the same dose of RGX-314 resulted in similar expression of anti-VEGF Fab and similar suppression of VEGF-induced vascular leakage.

engagement.model: Rat subretinal/suprachoroidal RGX-314 with VEGF-induced vascular leakage
engagement.magnitude_basis: RGX-314 Fab protein in ocular fluid
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; registry results (2023-05-16) do not report aqueous protein, so year is the Lancet epub.
engagement.note: Phase 1/2a: subretinal RGX-314 at 6e10 gc/eye or more gave sustained aqueous RGX-314 protein, as the rat expression data predicted.
engagement.quote: Doses of 6 × 1010 genome copies or higher resulted in sustained concentrations of RGX-314 protein in aqueous humour and stable or improved BCVA and central retinal thickness with few or no supplemental anti-VEGF-A injections in most participants.
engagement.judgement: Paired, not stated. Ding 2019 appeared after phase 1 dosing began (2017) but before protein data were published; treated as prospective (retrodiction false), low risk because transgene expression is not tuned to patient results.

efficacy.model: Rat subretinal/suprachoroidal RGX-314 with VEGF-induced vascular leakage
efficacy.confidence_note: Phase 3 status from sponsor news (topline expected Q4 2026); not found reported as of search.
efficacy.note: Rat model predicted suppression of VEGF-driven leakage; phase 1/2a primary endpoint was safety; ATMOSPHERE/ASCENT topline expected Q4 2026.
efficacy.quote: Compared with subretinal injection in rats of RGX-314, an AAV8 vector expressing an anti-VEGF Fab, suprachoroidal injection of the same dose of RGX-314 resulted in similar expression of anti-VEGF Fab and similar suppression of VEGF-induced vascular leakage.
efficacy.judgement: CRT/BCVA in the phase 1/2a were secondary in an uncontrolled study whose primary outcome was safety, so no efficacy comparison is scored.
